question:
Which of the following pairs of 'soil – characteristics' is correct?
I. Sandy – proportion of fine particles is relatively higher
II. Clayey – greater proportion of big particles
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neither I nor II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sandy soil is composed mainly of large, coarse particles with very little fine material; it has large pore spaces, drains water quickly and has low water-retention capacity. (बलुई मिट्टी — मोटे कणों की अधिकता)

 

• Statement I says sandy soil has a relatively higher proportion of fine particles, which is the opposite of reality — so Statement I is incorrect.

 

• Clayey soil is composed mainly of very fine particles tightly packed together, giving it high water-retention capacity and poor drainage — not big/coarse particles.

 

• Statement II says clayey soil has a greater proportion of big particles, which is also the opposite of reality — so Statement II is incorrect too.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Loamy soil, a mixture of sand, silt and clay in balanced proportion, is considered ideal for agriculture because it combines good drainage with good water/nutrient retention.

 

• Soil texture (proportion of sand, silt, clay) determines porosity, water-holding capacity and aeration, all of which affect crop suitability.

 

NOTE

 

• Only I (Option 1): Wrong, because Statement I itself is factually incorrect — sandy soil has more coarse particles, not fine ones.

 

• Both I and II (Option 3): Wrong, because both statements individually misstate the actual particle composition of sandy and clayey soils.

 

• Only II (Option 4): Wrong, because Statement II itself is factually incorrect — clayey soil has more fine particles, not big ones.

question: Malic Acid is found in which of the following substances?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Apple.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Malic acid is a naturally occurring organic (dicarboxylic) acid that gives apples their characteristic tart taste, and is therefore also called "apple acid". (मैलिक अम्ल — सेब में पाया जाता है)

 

• It is also found in smaller amounts in other fruits such as grapes, cherries and apricots, and is widely used as a food additive/flavouring agent (E296).

 

• Chemically, it is 2-hydroxybutanedioic acid, an intermediate compound in the citric acid (Krebs) cycle of cellular respiration.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Common acid–source pairs frequently asked in exams: Citric acid — citrus fruits (lemon, orange); Tartaric acid — tamarind, grapes; Acetic acid — vinegar; Formic acid — ant/bee sting, nettle sting; Lactic acid — sour milk/curd; Oxalic acid — spinach, tomato.

 

NOTE

 

• Vinegar (Option 2): Contains acetic acid, not malic acid.

 

• Ant's sting (Option 3): Contains formic acid (methanoic acid), which causes the burning/itching sensation.

 

• Tamarind (Option 4): Contains mainly tartaric acid, not malic acid.

question: ______ became the first bank to get Reserve Bank of India’s approval for rupee trade.
solution_text:
The correct answer is UCO Bank.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In July 2022, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) issued guidelines allowing rupee-denominated international trade settlement through Special Rupee Vostro Accounts, mainly to facilitate trade with countries like Russia amid sanctions.

 

• UCO Bank became the first bank to receive RBI's approval to open such a Special Vostro Account for settling trade in Indian rupees. (यूको बैंक — रुपये में व्यापार निपटान के लिए RBI की पहली मंज़ूरी)

 

• This mechanism allows Indian exporters/importers to invoice, pay and settle trade in INR instead of a foreign currency such as the US dollar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other banks such as IndusInd Bank, SBI and Union Bank of India also later received RBI approval to open similar special rupee vostro accounts.

 

• The rupee trade settlement mechanism is part of India's broader push toward internationalisation of the rupee and reducing dependence on hard currencies for bilateral trade.

 

NOTE

 

• SBI Bank (Option 1): India's largest public sector bank; it also later got approval for rupee vostro accounts, but was not the first.

 

• Axis Bank (Option 2): A private sector bank not associated with being the first to get this particular RBI approval.

 

• ICICI Bank (Option 4): A major private sector bank, but it was not the first to receive this RBI approval for rupee trade.

question: Ugadi is a Telugu festival celebrated on the occasion of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Telugu new year.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ugadi (also called Yugadi) marks the Telugu New Year, celebrated by people of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana on the first day of the Chaitra month of the Hindu lunisolar calendar. (उगादी — तेलुगु नव वर्ष)

 

• The word "Ugadi" is derived from "Yuga" (era) and "Adi" (beginning), meaning "the beginning of a new era/age".

 

• It is celebrated with the preparation of "Ugadi Pachadi", a dish combining six tastes (sweet, sour, salty, bitter, spicy, tangy) symbolising the different phases/emotions of life in the year ahead.

 

• The same day is celebrated as Gudi Padwa in Maharashtra and Cheti Chand by the Sindhi community.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Regional New Year festivals in India: Baisakhi (Punjab), Puthandu (Tamil Nadu), Vishu (Kerala), Bihu (Assam) — all generally fall around mid-April, in the same broad spring-harvest season as Ugadi.

 

NOTE

 

• Birth of lord Krishna (Option 1): This is celebrated as Janmashtami, not Ugadi.

 

• Birth of lord Rama (Option 2): This is celebrated as Ram Navami, which actually falls a few days after Ugadi in the same Chaitra month, but is a distinct festival.

 

• Coming of monsoon (Option 3): There is no major festival specifically marking the onset of monsoon called Ugadi; Ugadi is a New Year festival, not a monsoon festival.

question: Which Indian city is also known as Queen of Deccan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pune.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pune, located on the Deccan Plateau in Maharashtra, is popularly known as the "Queen of the Deccan" (also called the "Oxford of the East" for its educational institutions). (पुणे — दक्कन की रानी)

 

• It was historically the seat of power of the Peshwas (Maratha Empire administrators) and remains an important cultural, educational and IT hub of Maharashtra.

 

• The city sits at the confluence of the Mula and Mutha rivers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Indian city nicknames often asked in exams: Ahmedabad — "Manchester of India"; Amritsar — "Golden City"; Bengaluru — "Silicon Valley of India" / "Garden City"; Jaipur — "Pink City".

 

NOTE

 

• Ahmedabad (Option 1): Known as the "Manchester of India" due to its textile industry, not "Queen of the Deccan".

 

• Amritsar (Option 3): Known as the "Golden City", home to the Golden Temple; located in Punjab, not on the Deccan Plateau.

 

• Puducherry (Option 4): A former French colonial territory, sometimes called the "French Riviera of the East", not associated with the Deccan Plateau nickname.

question: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Act added the Right to Education to the Indian constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 86th.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 inserted Article 21A into Part III (Fundamental Rights) of the Constitution, making free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years a Fundamental Right. (86वां संविधान संशोधन — शिक्षा का अधिकार)

 

• The same amendment also added a corresponding Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(k), requiring parents/guardians to provide opportunities for education to their children/wards aged 6–14.

 

• It led to the enactment of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, which came into force on 1 April 2010 to operationalise Article 21A.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Before the 86th Amendment, the Right to Education existed only as a Directive Principle of State Policy under Article 45 ("free and compulsory education for children until they complete the age of fourteen years"), which was non-justiciable.

 

• After the 86th Amendment, Article 45 was reworded to focus on early childhood care and education for children below 6 years.

 

NOTE

 

• 85th Amendment (Option 1): Dealt with consequential seniority in promotions for SC/ST government employees (2001).

 

• 88th Amendment (Option 2): Inserted Article 268A relating to service tax, and amended the Union and State Lists (2003).

 

• 87th Amendment (Option 3): Related to the readjustment/delimitation of constituencies on the basis of the 2001 census (2003).

question:
In which of the following ways, aggregate demand function is related to consumption function?
I. They have the same slope C.
II. The aggregate demand function is parallel to the consumption function.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the basic Keynesian two-sector model, the Aggregate Demand function is AD = C + I, where C is the consumption function (C = a + bY) and I is autonomous (constant) investment. (कुल मांग फलन — उपभोग फलन के समांतर)

 

• Since investment I is treated as a constant (autonomous), adding it to the consumption function only shifts the line vertically upward by a fixed amount — it does not change the slope.

 

• The slope of both the consumption function and the aggregate demand function is the Marginal Propensity to Consume (MPC) = b, so Statement I (same slope) is correct.

 

• Because the two lines have the same slope but differ only by the constant vertical shift (I), the AD curve is parallel to the C curve — so Statement II is also correct.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The point where the Aggregate Demand curve intersects the 45° line (AD = Y) gives the equilibrium level of income in the simple Keynesian income-determination model.

 

• If government spending (G) is added, AD = C + I + G, and the curve shifts up further but again remains parallel, since G too is treated as autonomous.

 

NOTE

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 1): Incorrect, because both statements are actually true under the standard Keynesian assumption of autonomous investment.

 

• Only II (Option 2): Incorrect, because Statement I (same slope) is also true, not false.

 

• Only I (Option 3): Incorrect, because Statement II (parallel curves) is also true, not false.

question: ________, a 500-year-old dance form, is an Indian Classical dance that developed from the Vaishnavite monasteries of Assam.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sattriya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sattriya dance was introduced in the 15th century by the Assamese Vaishnavite saint-reformer Srimanta Sankardev as part of the Bhakti movement. (सत्रीया नृत्य — असम की वैष्णव मठ परंपरा)

 

• It developed and was traditionally preserved within the "sattras" — Vaishnavite monasteries of Assam — as a medium to propagate the Vaishnavite faith through dance-drama performances.

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi granted Sattriya the status of a classical dance of India in 2000, making it the 8th classical dance form to be officially recognised.

 

• It traditionally combines devotional themes (based on the lives of Krishna and Vishnu) with elaborate costume, mask work and music, and was originally performed only by male monks (bhokots) inside the monasteries.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's recognised classical dance forms include: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), and Sattriya (Assam).

 

NOTE

 

• Kuchipudi (Option 1): A classical dance form of Andhra Pradesh, rooted in Hindu Vaishnavite tradition but performed in temple villages, not Assamese sattras.

 

• Bharatnatyam (Option 2): A classical dance form that originated in the temples of Tamil Nadu, not associated with Assam.

 

• Mohiniattam (Option 4): A classical dance form of Kerala, characterised by graceful, swaying movements; unrelated to the Assamese Vaishnavite monasteries.

question: Who is famously known as the Tiger of Mysore?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tipu Sultan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tipu Sultan, the ruler of the Kingdom of Mysore, is famously known as the "Tiger of Mysore" for his fierce resistance to British expansion in South India. (टीपू सुल्तान — मैसूर का शेर)

 

• He was the son of Hyder Ali and fought the Second, Third and Fourth Anglo-Mysore Wars against the British East India Company.

 

• He died fighting the British at the Battle of Seringapatam (1799), in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War, defending his capital Srirangapatna.

 

• He was known for military innovations, including early use of iron-cased rockets (Mysorean rockets), which influenced later British rocket artillery.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tipu Sultan adopted the tiger as the royal emblem of Mysore, seen on his throne, weapons, flags and even his mechanical toy "Tipu's Tiger" (depicting a tiger mauling a European soldier), now displayed in London's Victoria and Albert Museum.

 

NOTE

 

• Baji Rao I (Option 1): A famous Maratha Peshwa, known as a brilliant military general, but not called "Tiger of Mysore".

 

• Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah (Option 3): A 20th-century political leader of Jammu & Kashmir, known as "Sher-e-Kashmir" (Lion of Kashmir), not connected to Mysore.

 

• Asaf Jah I (Option 4): Founder of the Hyderabad (Nizam) dynasty, unrelated to Mysore.

question: What is the venue for 4th Edition of Khelo India Youth Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Haryana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 4th edition of the Khelo India Youth Games (2021 edition) was hosted by Haryana, with Panchkula as the main venue. (खेलो इंडिया यूथ गेम्स — चौथा संस्करण, हरियाणा)

 

• Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the Games were postponed and eventually held from 4–13 June 2022.

 

• They were formally launched/inaugurated by then Union Home Minister Amit Shah.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Khelo India Youth Games host history: 1st edition (2018) — New Delhi; 2nd edition (2019) — Pune, Maharashtra; 3rd edition (2021, held Jan–Feb 2021) — Guwahati, Assam; 4th edition (2021, held June 2022) — Panchkula, Haryana.

 

• The Khelo India scheme aims to revive sports culture in India at the grassroots level by identifying and nurturing young sporting talent.

 

NOTE

 

• Maharashtra (Option 1): Hosted the 2nd edition of the Khelo India Youth Games (Pune, 2019), not the 4th.

 

• Delhi (Option 2): Hosted the 1st edition of the Khelo India (School) Games in 2018, not the 4th.

 

• Gujarat (Option 3): Hosted the Khelo India University Games, a separate event, not the 4th edition of the Youth Games.

question: Apple II is an example of ______ Generation of computer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fourth.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Fourth Generation of computers (1971 onward) is based on the microprocessor, which integrated the entire CPU onto a single chip using VLSI (Very Large Scale Integration) technology. (चौथी पीढ़ी के कंप्यूटर — माइक्रोप्रोसेसर आधारित)

 

• Apple II, launched in 1977 by Apple Computer (Steve Wozniak and Steve Jobs), was one of the first highly successful mass-produced microprocessor-based personal computers.

 

• Fourth-generation computers are smaller, faster, cheaper and more energy-efficient than earlier generations, and enabled the rise of personal computing.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Generations of computers (broad classification): 1st (1940s–50s) — vacuum tubes; 2nd (1950s–60s) — transistors; 3rd (1960s–70s) — integrated circuits (ICs); 4th (1970s–present) — microprocessors/VLSI; 5th (emerging) — Artificial Intelligence-based.

 

NOTE

 

• Third Generation (Option 1): Based on integrated circuits (ICs), roughly 1964–1971, predating the microprocessor used in Apple II.

 

• Second Generation (Option 2): Based on transistors, roughly 1956–1963, much earlier than the Apple II.

 

• First Generation (Option 3): Based on vacuum tubes, roughly 1940–1956, the earliest computing era, unrelated to microprocessor-based personal computers.

question: What is the full form of HTTP?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hyper Text Transfer Protocol.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• HTTP stands for "Hyper Text Transfer Protocol", the foundational application-layer protocol used for transferring data (web pages) over the World Wide Web. (HTTP — हाइपर टेक्स्ट ट्रांसफर प्रोटोकॉल)

 

• It defines how messages are formatted and transmitted between web browsers (clients) and web servers, and how servers respond to various commands (GET, POST, etc.).

 

• HTTPS (HTTP Secure) is the encrypted version of HTTP, using SSL/TLS to secure data transmission, commonly used for sensitive transactions like banking and shopping.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• HTTP was developed by Tim Berners-Lee at CERN, along with HTML and URLs, forming the core technologies of the World Wide Web.

 

• Other common internet protocol full forms: FTP — File Transfer Protocol; SMTP — Simple Mail Transfer Protocol; TCP/IP — Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol.

 

NOTE

 

• High Text Transmission Protocol (Option 1): Incorrect — uses the wrong words "High" and "Transmission" instead of "Hyper" and "Transfer".

 

• Hyper Text Transmission Protocol (Option 2): Incorrect — "Hyper Text" is right, but the correct word is "Transfer", not "Transmission".

 

• High Text Transfer Protocol (Option 4): Incorrect — "Transfer" is right, but the correct word is "Hyper Text", not "High Text".

question:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding the Lucknow Pact?
I. It was signed in the year 1916.
II. It was signed between the moderate and radical factions of Congress.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only I.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Lucknow Pact was signed in December 1916 at the joint session of the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League held in Lucknow — so Statement I is correct. (लखनऊ समझौता — दिसंबर 1916)

 

• The Lucknow Pact was actually an agreement between the Indian National Congress and the All India Muslim League, under which the Congress accepted the principle of separate electorates for Muslims in return for League support for self-government demands — it was not an agreement between the moderate and radical (extremist) factions of the Congress, so Statement II is incorrect.

 

• The reunification of the moderate and extremist factions of the Congress (who had split at the Surat Session, 1907) did happen at this same 1916 Lucknow Congress session, but that reunion was a separate development, not what the "Lucknow Pact" itself refers to.

 

• The pact was negotiated with leaders like Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Muhammad Ali Jinnah (then a Congress-League bridge leader), and marked a rare moment of Hindu-Muslim political unity before independence.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Lucknow Pact is often studied alongside the growth of separate electorates (first introduced by the Morley-Minto Reforms, 1909), a provision that later had long-term consequences for communal politics in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Both I and II (Option 1): Incorrect, because Statement II wrongly describes the Lucknow Pact as an intra-Congress agreement rather than a Congress-Muslim League agreement.

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 2): Incorrect, because Statement I (the 1916 date) is factually correct.

 

• Only II (Option 4): Incorrect, because it is Statement I, not Statement II, that is true.

question: Which of the following Airport become 1st airport in India to be run entirely on hydro and solar energy?
option_4: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport, Mumbai
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indira Gandhi International Airport, Delhi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Indira Gandhi International Airport (IGIA), Delhi, operated by DIAL (a GMR-led consortium), became India's first airport to run entirely on hydro and solar power. (इंदिरा गांधी अंतरराष्ट्रीय हवाई अड्डा — जल और सौर ऊर्जा)

 

• This was achieved through a mix of on-site solar power plants and hydroelectric power sourced from Himachal Pradesh/Uttarakhand-based hydro projects via power purchase agreements.

 

• The airport was also recognised as the first airport in the Asia-Pacific region to be powered entirely by renewable (hydro + solar) energy for its terminal operations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Cochin International Airport (Kerala) was earlier recognised as the world's first fully solar-powered airport (2015) — a related but distinct milestone from Delhi's "hydro + solar" achievement.

 

• This shift supports India's broader push toward carbon-neutral airport operations and renewable energy adoption in aviation infrastructure.

 

NOTE

 

• Chennai International Airport (Option 2): Has undertaken solar energy initiatives, but was not the first to run entirely on hydro and solar power.

 

• Dabolim Airport, Goa (Option 3): A major airport in Goa, but not recognised for this particular renewable-energy milestone.

 

• Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport, Mumbai (Option 4): India's second-busiest airport, but not the first to achieve fully hydro-and-solar-powered operations.

question: Which of the following statements regarding the deccan plateau is NOT correct?
option_1: The Deccan Plateau is higher in the west and slopes gently eastwards.
option_2: The Deccan Plateau is a triangular landmass.
option_3: An extension of the Plateau is also visible in the northeast.
option_4: The Satpura range flanks its broad base in the west.
solution_text:
The correct answer (the statement that is NOT correct) is "The Satpura range flanks its broad base in the west."

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Deccan Plateau is a large triangular tableland covering most of peninsular India south of the Narmada river — so the statement that it is a triangular landmass is correct. (दक्कन का पठार — त्रिभुजाकार भू-भाग)

 

• It is higher in the west (due to the Western Ghats) and slopes gently eastwards, which is why most major peninsular rivers (Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri) flow from west to east into the Bay of Bengal — this statement is correct.

 

• An extension of the plateau is visible in the northeast in the form of the Meghalaya (Shillong) Plateau and Karbi Anglong Plateau, separated from the main Deccan block by the Rajmahal Hills and the Ganga-Brahmaputra plains — this statement is also correct.

 

• The Satpura Range, along with the Vindhya Range, flanks the Deccan Plateau's broad base in the north, not the west — the plateau's western edge is flanked by the Western Ghats (Sahyadri), so this statement is factually incorrect, making it the answer to this "NOT correct" question.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Deccan Plateau is bounded by the Western Ghats on the west, the Eastern Ghats on the east, and the Satpura–Vindhya–Mahadeo–Maikal ranges on the north.

 

• The plateau is composed mainly of basaltic (Deccan Trap) rock, formed by volcanic activity around 66 million years ago, giving rise to fertile black (regur) soil in much of Maharashtra.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (higher in west, slopes eastward): A correct statement about the plateau's overall topography and drainage pattern.

 

• Option 2 (triangular landmass): A correct, standard geographical description of the Deccan Plateau's shape.

 

• Option 3 (extension visible in northeast): A correct statement, referring to the Meghalaya/Karbi Anglong Plateau as a detached northeastern extension.

question:
Which of the following pair of "player – sports" is correct?
I. Lovlina Borgohain – Boxing
II. Nikhat Zareen – Wrestling
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only I.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lovlina Borgohain is an Indian boxer from Assam who won the bronze medal in the women's welterweight category at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics — so Statement I is correct. (लवलीना बोरगोहेन — मुक्केबाज़)

 

• Nikhat Zareen is also an Indian boxer, not a wrestler; she won the gold medal at the 2022 IBA Women's World Boxing Championships in the flyweight category — so Statement II (which calls her sport "Wrestling") is incorrect.

 

• Both athletes compete in the same sport, boxing, representing India at top international boxing tournaments.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable Indian women boxers include Mary Kom (six-time World Champion, Olympic bronze medallist) and Sarita Devi.

 

• Well-known Indian women wrestlers (a different sport) include Sakshi Malik, Vinesh Phogat and Geeta/Babita Phogat.

 

NOTE

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 1): Incorrect, because Statement I correctly pairs Lovlina Borgohain with boxing.

 

• Both I and II (Option 2): Incorrect, because Statement II wrongly labels Nikhat Zareen's sport as wrestling instead of boxing.

 

• Only II (Option 3): Incorrect, because it is Statement I, not Statement II, that is accurate.

question: Which country’s moon mission has mapped out the global distribution of sodium on the Moon’s surface in October 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's Chandrayaan-2 orbiter, still operational around the Moon, used its CLASS (Chandrayaan-2 Large Area Soft X-ray Spectrometer) instrument to map the global distribution of sodium on the lunar surface for the first time, with findings reported around October 2022. (चंद्रयान-2 — चंद्रमा पर सोडियम का मानचित्रण)

 

• This was achieved by studying X-ray fluorescence lines emitted from the lunar surface when it is exposed to solar X-rays, allowing scientists to detect the sodium signature directly (rather than only in the Moon's thin exosphere, as done by earlier missions).

 

• The finding suggested sodium exists as a surface constituent (possibly as sodium-bearing minerals like feldspar) and could help understand the Moon's thin, tenuous atmosphere (exosphere).

 

• Chandrayaan-2, launched by ISRO in July 2019, consists of an orbiter, lander (Vikram) and rover (Pragyan); while the lander crashed, the orbiter has continued to function successfully and deliver valuable scientific data.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chandrayaan-2's orbiter carries eight scientific instruments, including the Dual-frequency Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), which helped confirm the presence of water-ice in permanently shadowed polar regions.

 

• India followed up with the successful Chandrayaan-3 mission (soft-landed near the lunar south pole in August 2023), building on Chandrayaan-2's data and heritage.

 

NOTE

 

• United States of America (Option 1): NASA has conducted extensive lunar missions (e.g., LRO, Artemis), but the sodium-mapping finding referred to here is attributed to India's Chandrayaan-2, not a US mission.

 

• Russia (Option 2): Russia's Luna missions (historic and the 2023 Luna-25 attempt) are not associated with this particular sodium-mapping discovery.

 

• China (Option 4): China's Chang'e lunar missions have made other notable discoveries (e.g., far-side landing, sample return), but not this specific sodium-distribution mapping.

question: In which part of the Indian constitution are the provisions related to panchayat mentioned?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Part IX.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Part IX of the Indian Constitution, titled "The Panchayats" (Articles 243 to 243-O), was inserted by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992. (भाग IX — पंचायत)

 

• It provides for the establishment of a three-tier Panchayati Raj system: Gram Panchayat (village level), Panchayat Samiti (intermediate/block level) and Zila Parishad (district level).

 

• The Amendment also added the Eleventh Schedule, listing 29 subjects that can be devolved to Panchayats, and mandated regular elections, reservation of seats for SC/ST and women, and State Election Commissions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part IXA (Articles 243P–243ZG), added by the 74th Amendment Act, 1992, deals with Municipalities (urban local self-government), and is accompanied by the Twelfth Schedule.

 

• Together, the 73rd and 74th Amendments form the constitutional basis for local self-governance in rural and urban India respectively.

 

NOTE

 

• Part XI (Option 1): Deals with relations between the Union and the States (legislative, administrative relations), not Panchayats.

 

• Part IX A (Option 3): Deals with Municipalities, not Panchayats — often confused with Part IX because of the similar numbering and related subject matter.

 

• Part X (Option 4): Deals with the administration of Scheduled and Tribal Areas, not Panchayats.

question: Who was the first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnam Malleswari.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Karnam Malleswari, an Indian weightlifter, won the bronze medal in the 69 kg category at the 2000 Sydney Olympics, becoming the first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal. (कर्णम मल्लेश्वरी — ओलंपिक पदक जीतने वाली पहली भारतीय महिला)

 

• She remains one of only a small number of Indian weightlifters to achieve Olympic success and was honoured with the Padma Shri, Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna and Arjuna Award.

 

• Her achievement predates other well-known Indian women Olympic medallists such as Saina Nehwal (badminton, 2012 bronze) and Sakshi Malik (wrestling, 2016 bronze).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's first-ever individual Olympic medal (of any gender) was won by wrestler K. D. Jadhav (bronze, 1952 Helsinki Olympics).

 

• Other pioneering Indian women in Olympic sport: P. T. Usha narrowly missed a medal by 1/100th of a second in the 400m hurdles at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics.

 

NOTE

 

• Neelamshetty Appanna (Option 1): Not a recognised Olympic medallist; included here as a distractor name.

 

• Saina Nehwal (Option 3): Won India's first Olympic medal in badminton (bronze, London 2012), but was not the first Indian woman overall to win an Olympic medal.

 

• Sakshi Malik (Option 4): Won a bronze medal in wrestling at the 2016 Rio Olympics, well after Karnam Malleswari's 2000 medal.

question: The Young Bengal Movement was founded by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Henry Louis Vivian Derozio.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Henry Louis Vivian Derozio (1809–1831), a young Anglo-Indian teacher at Hindu College, Calcutta, founded and inspired the Young Bengal Movement in the late 1820s. (हेनरी लुई विवियन डेरोज़ियो — यंग बंगाल आंदोलन)

 

• His followers, called the "Derozians", were radical thinkers who questioned orthodox Hindu religious and social customs, championed free thought, rationalism, and criticised superstition, caste rigidity and idolatry.

 

• Derozio also founded the "Academic Association" in 1828 as a platform to discuss and debate radical, reformist and revolutionary ideas among his students.

 

• Despite being dismissed from Hindu College in 1831 (partly due to controversy over his radical teachings) and dying young of cholera the same year, his ideas had a lasting influence on the Bengal Renaissance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Young Bengal Movement is often seen as a precursor to later socio-religious reform movements in Bengal, including the work of the Brahmo Samaj.

 

• Notable Derozians included Krishna Mohan Banerjee, Ramgopal Ghosh and Dakshinaranjan Mukherjee.

 

NOTE

 

• Dayanand Saraswati (Option 2): Founded the Arya Samaj (1875), a reform movement based in North India, unrelated to Young Bengal.

 

• Lala Hansraj (Option 3): An Arya Samaj leader associated with the DAV (Dayanand Anglo-Vedic) educational movement in Punjab, not Young Bengal.

 

• Keshab Chandra Sen (Option 4): A prominent leader of the Brahmo Samaj, active later in the 19th century, not the founder of Young Bengal.

question: Who won the women’s singles title at the US Open 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Iga Swiatek.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Iga Swiatek of Poland won the women's singles title at the 2022 US Open, defeating Ons Jabeur of Tunisia in the final. (इगा स्विऑटेक — यूएस ओपन 2022 महिला एकल विजेता)

 

• This was Swiatek's third Grand Slam singles title overall (after two French Open titles, 2020 and 2022) and her first US Open title.

 

• With this win, she solidified her position as the World No. 1 in women's tennis rankings.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2022 US Open was notably Serena Williams' final professional tournament, as she announced her retirement ("evolution" away from tennis) around this event, though she did not win the title that year.

 

• The men's singles title at the 2022 US Open was won by Carlos Alcaraz of Spain, who became the youngest World No. 1 in ATP history at the time.

 

NOTE

 

• Serena Williams (Option 2): A 23-time Grand Slam singles champion who played her farewell tournament at the 2022 US Open but lost in the third round, not the champion that year.

 

• Venus Williams (Option 3): Serena's sister and a multiple Grand Slam champion, but did not win the 2022 US Open women's singles title.

 

• Ons Jabeur (Option 4): Reached the final of the 2022 US Open but lost to Iga Swiatek, finishing as the runner-up.

question: Which of the following is NOT an inner planet of our solar system?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jupiter.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The inner (terrestrial) planets of the solar system — Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars — are small, rocky, dense planets located closer to the Sun, inside the asteroid belt. (आंतरिक ग्रह — बुध, शुक्र, पृथ्वी, मंगल)

 

• Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system and is classified as an outer planet / gas giant, located beyond the asteroid belt, composed mainly of hydrogen and helium.

 

• The outer planets are Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune — all gas giants or ice giants, much larger and less dense than the inner planets.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The asteroid belt, located between Mars and Jupiter, is generally considered the dividing line between the inner (terrestrial) and outer (giant) planets.

 

• Jupiter has a prominent storm system, the Great Red Spot, and is known for its large number of moons, including the four large Galilean moons: Io, Europa, Ganymede and Callisto.

 

NOTE

 

• Mars (Option 1): A rocky, terrestrial planet and the fourth planet from the Sun — correctly classified as an inner planet.

 

• Venus (Option 2): A rocky, terrestrial planet and the second planet from the Sun — correctly classified as an inner planet.

 

• Mercury (Option 3): The smallest and closest planet to the Sun, rocky in composition — correctly classified as an inner planet.

question: In the XXI phase of sale of electoral bonds can be only purchase from which of the following institution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is SBI.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under the Electoral Bond Scheme, 2018, notified by the Government of India, State Bank of India (SBI) is the sole authorised bank permitted to issue and encash Electoral Bonds. (चुनावी बॉन्ड — केवल भारतीय स्टेट बैंक से खरीदे जा सकते हैं)

 

• Electoral bonds are interest-free bearer instruments used by individuals/companies to donate money to political parties, purchasable at specified SBI branches during notified sale windows (each "phase").

 

• Each phase of sale is announced periodically by the government (e.g., typically for 10 days each in January, April, July and October, with an additional 30-day window in Lok Sabha election years), and can only be bought from SBI's designated branches, using KYC-compliant bank accounts.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Electoral Bond Scheme faced significant legal challenges over concerns of donor anonymity and transparency in political funding; the Supreme Court of India struck down the scheme as unconstitutional in February 2024 (a later development after this exam's reference date).

 

• Bonds are sold in denominations ranging from ₹1,000 to ₹1 crore and must be encashed by the receiving political party within 15 days of issue.

 

NOTE

 

• NITI Aayog (Option 1): India's policy think tank responsible for development planning, with no role in electoral bond sales.

 

• RBI (Option 2): India's central bank, which regulates the banking system, but does not itself sell electoral bonds — this role is specifically assigned to SBI.

 

• SEBI (Option 3): India's securities market regulator, unrelated to the sale/encashment of electoral bonds.

question: According to which of the following laws, the pressure of a mixture of gases is equal to the sum of the partial pressures of the component gases?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dalton's Law.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dalton's Law of Partial Pressures, proposed by John Dalton, states that the total pressure exerted by a mixture of non-reacting gases equals the sum of the partial pressures of each individual gas in the mixture. (डाल्टन का आंशिक दाब का नियम)

 

• Mathematically: P(total) = P1 + P2 + P3 + ..., where each Pi is the pressure that gas i would exert if it alone occupied the same volume at the same temperature.

 

• This law is widely applied in fields like respiratory physiology (partial pressure of oxygen/carbon dioxide in blood/lungs) and scuba diving (gas mixture calculations).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Related gas laws often confused with each other: Boyle's Law (P ∝ 1/V at constant T), Charles' Law (V ∝ T at constant P), Graham's Law (rate of diffusion ∝ 1/√molar mass), Avogadro's Law (equal volumes of gases at same T & P contain equal number of moles).

 

NOTE

 

• Charles' Law (Option 1): States that at constant pressure, the volume of a gas is directly proportional to its absolute temperature — unrelated to partial pressures of a gas mixture.

 

• Boyle's Law (Option 2): States that at constant temperature, the pressure of a gas is inversely proportional to its volume — describes a single gas, not a mixture's partial pressures.

 

• Graham's Law (Option 4): States that the rate of diffusion/effusion of a gas is inversely proportional to the square root of its molar mass — concerns diffusion rate, not partial pressures.

question: El Nino is a name given to the periodic development of a warm ocean current along the coast of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Peru.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• El Niño refers to the periodic warming of surface waters in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean, observed along the coast of Peru (and Ecuador). (एल नीनो — पेरू तट के पास गर्म समुद्री धारा)

 

• The name "El Niño" (Spanish for "the little boy"/"Christ child") was originally given by Peruvian fishermen, as the warm current typically appeared around Christmas time, disrupting the usual cold, nutrient-rich Peru (Humboldt) Current and reducing fish catches.

 

• El Niño is part of the broader El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) climate pattern, which affects global weather, including a weakening of the Indian monsoon in El Niño years.

 

• Its opposite phase, characterised by unusually cool ocean temperatures in the same region, is called La Niña.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Normally, the Peru (Humboldt) Current brings cold, nutrient-rich water northward along the South American coast, supporting rich fisheries; El Niño temporarily disrupts this pattern.

 

• El Niño events typically recur every 2 to 7 years and can last from several months to over a year, with wide-ranging global climatic impacts including droughts, floods and altered monsoon patterns.

 

NOTE

 

• Columbia (Option 1): A South American country (correctly spelled Colombia) further north, not the location associated with the naming/observation of El Niño.

 

• Chile (Option 3): A South American country to the south of Peru; while affected by ENSO patterns, El Niño is specifically named for and first identified along the coast of Peru.

 

• Bolivia (Option 4): A landlocked South American country with no coastline, so it cannot be the coast referenced in the question.
